beats: Hook (line_qc_out_unfinished_road, then the cover): forty years in, nobody has found a law of physics that forbids a useful quantum computer; so what could still stop it, and what should a computer scientist build next? The road has no wall across it, only stretches not yet built. Cast: the series finale brings back the QC01 cast (her first lecture), the physicist (bald with a fluffy fringe, bushy moustache, goggles pushed up, lab coat) and the student (tuft of hair, round glasses, striped T-shirt, messenger bag); both invented. No lecturer figure anywhere and never her likeness: her voice carries this part (math none, heavier on her clips). No race framing of any kind; name no company, lab or funding programme.

What could make it fail (Q24-02 p40, slide only; tape it): (1) error correction assumes errors do not grow with the number of qubits (line_qc_out_crowded_cafe: the more guests, the louder everyone must talk); (2) bigger chips may lose quality, addressability and gate fidelity (reuse line_qc_pitch_souffle from QC01-04).

Quadratic speed-ups vs overhead (Q24-13 14:39-15:59, clip 15:06-15:59): a shortcut that needs only the square root of the steps does not pay when every error-corrected step is far slower, unless the job is enormous (line_qc_out_shortcut_snail; FACTS: Babbush et al., PRX Quantum 2, 010103, 2021); exponential speed-ups survive the overhead (reuse line_qc_analog_toll_tunnel from QC01-03).

Quantum machine learning on classical data (Q24-13 15:59-17:52): after error-correction overhead the speed-up is unproven, and classical machine learning is already strong with approximations (line_qc_out_peeler_jury: the judge has not decided); learning methods for quantum problems such as chemistry simulation are a different, still active line (her distinction at 16:00-16:40).
Near-term applications are still being looked for (Q25-01 52:20-53:45, her answer; the chat question is a student's: paraphrase it) (reuse line_qc_hier_compass_trail from QC01-06).

Directions (Q24-13 73:51-74:40): machine learning for quantum systems, for decoders, mapping and code design (line_qc_out_sheepdog_pens: the trained dog pens the sheep while the physicist chases one); software stacks for neutral-atom and photonic, measurement-based machines are new (Q24-13 75:00-77:00; the companies she names stay off screen and out of the narration) (line_qc_out_new_lab_shelves; reuse line_qc_hier_hybrid_lab). Never use Q24-13 65:58-73:51 (logistics, grading, remarks on chatbot-written reports).
Two kinds of research (clip Q24-13 77:19-77:46; Q25-03 51:29-52:22): improve a known solution, or open a new area (line_qc_out_two_researches).

Classical philosophy, quantum details (clip Q25-01 74:54-75:20): the same blueprint, built in new material with new tools (line_qc_out_brick_and_ice). Research that reaches industry (clip Q25-02 77:22-77:55; the compiler names in that window stay off screen).
Cover (line_qc_cover_09_01; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the student points along an unfinished road towards far mountains; the physicist shades his eyes beside the student.
